paper_title: Gated Attention for Large Language Models Non-linearity, Sparsity, and   Attention-Sink-Free
caption: Comparison of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across different gating configurations. Row 1 (Baseline): Significant massive activations and attention sinks emerge after the 6th layer. Row 2 (SDPA Gating): Reduced activations and no attention sinks observed. Row 3 (Value Layer Gating): Similar activations to Row 2 but with residual attention sinks. Rows 4–5 (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share and NS-sigmoid): Massive activations and attention sinks resemble the baseline.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: The figure illustrates the variation of first token attention scores across transformer layers in a baseline model. The horizontal axis, labeled “layer,” represents the layer index and is marked with integer values from 0 to 23, spaced at regular intervals of 1. The vertical axis, labeled “first token attention score,” is scaled linearly from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks and labels at intervals of 0.2. A horizontal dashed green line indicates the mean attention score, labeled as “mean: 0.467.” The primary data series, shown as a solid blue line with circular markers, depicts the first token attention score for each layer. At layer 0, the score begins near 0.05, rises to approximately 0.12 at layer 2, dips to about 0.08 at layer 4, then sharply increases to approximately 0.65 at layer 6. After layer 6, the score fluctuates between approximately 0.4 and 0.8, reaching a local peak of about 0.85 at layer 22 before declining to approximately 0.42 at layer 23. The green dashed line remains constant at 0.467 across all layers.
model_annotations.Chinese: This line chart displays the first token attention scores across layers for a baseline model, with the x-axis representing the layer number ranging from 0 to 25 in linear scale and the y-axis representing the first token attention score ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 in linear scale, with numerical tick marks spaced at intervals of 0.2. A solid blue line, labeled “first token attention score,” shows the per-layer attention values, starting near 0.05 at layer 0, rising to a peak of approximately 0.65 at layer 7, then fluctuating between roughly 0.4 and 0.7 until layer 22, where it peaks again at approximately 0.85, before declining to approximately 0.42 at layer 25. A dashed green horizontal line, labeled “mean: 0.467,” is drawn across the chart at the mean attention score, intersecting the blue line at multiple points, including near layer 10 and layer 25.

The y-axis, labeled “first token attention score,” is linearly scaled from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at regular intervals of 0.2, representing the normalized attention weight. A horizontal dashed green line, labeled “mean: 0.467,” spans the entire chart at the constant value of 0.467, serving as a reference for the mean attention score across all layers.
